mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -14.4 to -13.4 over the last four weeks, indicating a stable recovery trend that will continue its gradual upward trajectory into the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed four-week monotonic rise.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improved by nearly 2 points in the most recent week after being flat near -39 for three weeks; if this uptick exceeds a 1.5-point week-on-week threshold, it signals renewed commuting and errand travel that will lift RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 1.5 points week-on-week after at least two prior flat weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -39.3 to -37.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks following a TRANSIT week-on-week increase exceeding 1.5 points.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL continues its decline.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS values swing between -39.3 and -35.7 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a PARKS swing exceeding 3 points, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its trend from either single-series hypothesis when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise concurrently.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45 or WORKPLACES falls below -20 within a single week
evidence_refs: fact:current TRANSIT at -37.4 and WORKPLACES at -13.0 are well above these thresholds
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT or WORKPLACES crossing the specified restriction thresholds.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow 0.4 to 1.4 band over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a significant directional move in the next week that correlates strongly with GROCERY_PHARM changes, contradicting the no-push assumption.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state regime with no abrupt policy changes, the combination of declining RESIDENTIAL and rising WORKPLACES together signal a seasonal late-summer normalization of routines; this joint behavioral-activity shift will continue to incrementally raise RETAIL_REC on a one-week horizon as the two trends reinforce each other, but only while RESIDENTIAL stays below 6.5 and WORKPLACES stays above -14.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays below 6.5 and WORKPLACES stays above -14 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 5.9 and WORKPLACES at -13.0 in latest week both meet these conditions
